facts.text: Acceptance criteria are measurable conditions agreed before testing starts that determine whether a result is good enough; pass or fail criteria apply the same idea to an individual test.
facts.quote: Acceptance criteria are the measurable conditions, agreed before testing starts, that decide whether a result is good enough, and pass or fail criteria are the same idea applied to one test.

facts.text: A good acceptance criterion specifies a quantity, a threshold and the conditions under which the threshold applies.
facts.quote: A good acceptance criterion names a quantity, a threshold and the conditions

facts.text: An example acceptance criterion requires a machine reversing at 10 km/h or less on dry gravel to stop with at least 1.0 meter remaining in all 20 runs.
facts.quote: "in reverse at 10 km/h or less on dry gravel, the machine stops with at least 1.0 meter remaining, in all 20 runs"

facts.text: Scenario-level acceptance criteria judge a single maneuver using quantities such as stop gap, impact speed and warning lead time.
facts.quote: Scenario-level criteria judge one maneuver (stop gap, impact speed, warning lead time).

facts.text: Statistical acceptance criteria judge rates over time, such as false interventions per 1,000 operating hours.
facts.quote: Statistical criteria judge rates over time (false interventions per 1,000 operating hours).

facts.text: Model-credibility acceptance criteria judge the simulation itself, for example by requiring predicted stopping distance to be within a stated margin of the measured value on every anchor run.
facts.quote: Model-credibility criteria judge the simulation itself (predicted stopping distance within a stated margin of the measured value on every anchor run)

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires detection within 300 milliseconds.
facts.quote: ISO 16001 requires detection within 300 milliseconds.

facts.text: The South African mining specification MOSH requires a detection range of 200 meters.
facts.quote: The South African mining specification MOSH requires a 200 meter detection range

facts.text: The South African mining specification MOSH requires a warning 2.5 to 3.0 seconds before intervention.
facts.quote: a 2.5 to 3.0 second warning before intervention

facts.text: The South African mining specification MOSH requires stop gaps of 1.0 to 4.0 meters at speeds of 10 km/h or less, and 15 meters plus or minus 5 meters at speeds above 10 km/h.
facts.quote: stop gaps of 1.0 to 4.0 meters at 10 km/h or less and 15 meters plus or minus 5 meters above that

facts.text: The South African mining specification MOSH requires fail-to-safe within 500 milliseconds.
facts.quote: fail-to-safe within 500 milliseconds

facts.text: The South African mining specification MOSH requires “no false interventions and false warnings” at its laboratory gate.
facts.quote: "no false interventions and false warnings" at its laboratory gate

facts.text: No off-road standard or regulation specifies a value for false alarms or unnecessary brake events per operating hour.
facts.quote: But no off-road standard or regulation gives a value for false alarms or unnecessary brake events per operating hour.

facts.text: False-alarm and unnecessary-braking rate limits must be set as program-level criteria with separate tolerances for advisory warnings, urgent warnings, speed reduction and full braking, because an unnecessary advisory differs from an unnecessary emergency stop of a loaded machine.
facts.quote: These must be set as program-level criteria, with separate tolerances for advisory warnings, urgent warnings, speed reduction and full braking, because an unnecessary advisory is not the same as an unnecessary emergency stop of a loaded machine

facts.text: The booklet's metric list includes true-positive detection, dangerous misses, stopping margin, brake-command latency, availability and time in degraded mode.
facts.quote: The booklet's metric list runs from true-positive detection and dangerous misses to stopping margin, brake-command latency, availability and time in degraded mode

facts.text: Acceptance criteria should be set before results are seen.
facts.quote: Criteria are set before results are seen

facts.text: NASA's simulation standard requires program-defined acceptance criteria approved by technical authority.
facts.quote: NASA's simulation standard requires program-defined acceptance criteria approved by technical authority

facts.text: Acceptance criteria are to be derived from safety requirements and agreed before the main test campaign.
facts.quote: They are derived from the safety requirements and agreed before the main campaign

facts.text: Safety and productivity acceptance criteria should be set jointly: a “no false brakes” target pushes toward late or missed braking, whereas a detection-only target produces a machine that keeps stopping production.
facts.quote: Safety and productivity criteria are set jointly, because a "no false brakes" target pushes toward late or missed braking while a detection-only target produces a machine that keeps stopping production

facts.text: When hundreds of machine, weather and scenario cells are each checked at 95 percent confidence, some pass or fail by chance; primary claims should therefore be named in advance.
facts.quote: When hundreds of machine, weather and scenario cells are each checked at 95 percent confidence, some pass or fail by chance, so the primary claims are named in advance

facts.text: A test pass by a margin no larger than the model's uncertainty is not robust, so results should carry their tolerance.
facts.quote: A pass by a margin no larger than the model's uncertainty is not robust, so results carry their tolerance

facts.text: Skeptical reviewers ask which acceptance criteria were chosen before results were seen.
facts.quote: Skeptical reviewers ask directly: "What acceptance criteria were chosen before seeing results?"

facts.text: The program's four-month validation window fails if pass or fail metrics remain “to be decided” in 2027.
facts.quote: The four-month window fails if pass or fail metrics are still "to be decided" in 2027

facts.text: No off-road authority has committed to accept virtual evidence.
facts.quote: no off-road authority has committed to accept virtual evidence

facts.text: Acceptance criteria must specify how simulation results may be used, because no off-road authority has committed to accept virtual evidence.
facts.quote: since no off-road authority has committed to accept virtual evidence, the criteria must also say how simulation results may be used
